title: Level 2 (Intermediate) - D-23
notes:
West leads the ♥8 against 3NT. It's now or never for the ♥J and, when it holds, South's remaining ♥K doubleton will act as a second stopper as long as East can be kept off lead. South must play on diamonds to come close to 9 tricks. He can afford to lose a diamond trick as long as East does not gain the lead.

South should lead a low diamond from the dummy at trick 2. When East follows small, South should play the ♦9 from his hand. West is welcome to win this trick, but he cannot attack hearts profitably from his side of the table. South should win West's club return with dummy's ♣A and unblock the diamonds. South can now cross to the ♠K in order to cash dummy's 3 remaining diamond winners. The ♠A will be South's 9th trick.

If South had to play diamonds for 6 tricks, the percentage play would be to cash the ♦A and ♦K hoping for the ♦Q to drop. On this deal it would be wrong to play this way as East would win the ♦Q on the third round and lead a heart through South's ♥K to defeat 3NT. Given that South can afford to lose a diamond trick, he should take the recommended line in order to minimize the chances of having to lose that trick to East.
